items.title: OpenAI models helped researchers—operating as part of our Patch the Planet initiative—discover criti...
items.content:
OpenAI models helped researchers—operating as part of our Patch the Planet initiative—discover critical security flaws in PHP, an open-source programming language used to run an estimated 70% of websites.

Over the past two months, we led a coalition of maintainers, researchers, and security providers to prepare fixes and protections ahead of disclosure. This duration was necessary because the fix was quite intricate and required a major change to the PHP engine. Every site using PHP can now safely upgrade their version to stay secure, in addition to applying mitigations from various security vendors.

Due to the severity of these flaws and PHP’s widespread use, we consider this bug to be one of the most impactful vulnerabilities in recent memory. It also marks a new phase, where AI can find security bugs with internet-scale impact. 

This is an example of the Defender’s Window in action: to our knowledge, frontier AI was able to find this vulnerability ahead of attackers, giving defenders time to prepare.
https://t.co/TW3jrSbB3f

In our new benchmark AA-PersonalityBench, GPT-4o, Llama 4 Maverick, and GPT-3.5 Turbo, the three oldest models measured, rank highest on the Sycophantic personality trait. Grok 4.7, Claude Fable 5.1, and Inkling rank lowest

➤ @AIatMeta models are highly concentrated near the top: all five Meta models measured rank 65 or higher (Llama 4 Maverick 97, Muse Spark 1.3 87, Muse Glimmer 79, Muse Spark Open 76, Muse Wonder 65)

➤ @GoogleDeepMind models are spread out along the Sycophantic range: Gemini 3.1 Pro Preview ranks 89, Gemini 4 Argon 81, and Gemini 3.8 Flash 28, ranking from the top quartile to almost bottom quartile

➤ @spacexai's Grok 4.7 model ranks the lowest of all models measured. Congratulations @elonmusk!

items.title: An OpenAI model just helped find what the company calls "one of the most impactful security issues i...
items.content:
An OpenAI model just helped find what the company calls "one of the most impactful security issues in recent memory."

The target was PHP, the language behind WordPress and nearly 70% of websites.

Security firm Calif pointed GPT-5.6 Sol at PHP’s code, and it found a critical flaw that could let attackers take over a server without logging in. Wiz found the same bugs independently.

OpenAI then spent two months coordinating the response with PHP’s maintainers, Wiz and Cloudflare.

Patches dropped this morning after details leaked early, but any server that hasn’t updated is still exposed.

The National Security Agency told organizations that can’t update yet to take their systems offline.

items.content:
SITUATION EXPLAINED: Dario Amodei wrote nearly 2,000 words defending Anthropic against claims it's just racing to superintelligence.

• It started with Anthropic's leaked draft AI safety bill, which lets the government block a model only through a court and only for an imminent risk of 50+ deaths or $1B+ in damage
• Encode's @_NathanCalvin said that makes dangerous models harder to stop than under existing law, and Anthropic says it's revising the bill
• He then asked "What is Anthropic?" and concluded it's mainly racing to superintelligence, citing custom chips, $500B+ in compute, and Claude doing more of its own AI R&D
• Dario called the strategy a "race to the top" and listed 9 costly safety moves, like holding Mythos back for months, cutting off PRC-controlled firms, and the 5% public benefit fund
• He admitted some mistakes but wrote, "Even if I conceded every item in your list, I would happily hold up mine next to it"

@theojaffee: "Nathan points out Anthropic is not a purely profit-maximizing company, nor is it an AI safety org. It's a secret third thing that involves racing to superintelligence before their rivals can get there. And this seems like it's been the strategy of basically every AI company."

items.title: We've updated MLCR-AA, our leaderboard for Wisedocs' Medical Long Context Reasoning benchmark, with ...
items.content:
We've updated MLCR-AA, our leaderboard for Wisedocs' Medical Long Context Reasoning benchmark, with Claude Sonnet 5.5 and GPT-6 Astra now tied for the #1 score

We've updated how MLCR-AA prompts and grades models on @wisedocsai's benchmark, to better reflect how medical record review is done in practice. Models are now prompted as medical record reviewers, and asked to answer each part of a question in one paragraph with their conclusion and the supporting evidence from the record. Answers are graded by a new three-model judge panel, and we reviewed all 60 expert reference answers against their source records, refining 15.

Claude Sonnet 5.5 (max with fallback) from @AnthropicAI and GPT-6 Astra (max) from @OpenAI are tied at the top with 41.7%, followed by GPT-6.1 Sol (max) at 38.3%. Qwen3.8 2.4T A95B from @Alibaba_Qwen is the leading open weights model at 30.6%.

Key results from the updated MLCR-AA:

➤ Medical record review remains far from solved: an answer passes only when it is both complete and accurate, and no model passes more than 42% of questions and the median model passes under 15%

➤ Anthropic models lead on completeness, reaching the expert's conclusion with the right medical reasoning: Claude models hold the top 18 completeness scores across every model and effort level we tested, led by Claude Sonnet 5.5 (max with fallback) at 64.8%. The best non-Anthropic model is GPT-6 Astra (max) at 42.2%

➤ OpenAI models lead on accuracy, citing the record without exaggeration or hallucination: OpenAI models hold the top 27 accuracy scores, led by GPT-6.1 Sol (max) at 96.7%, but answer fewer questions completely: GPT-6.1 Sol (max) is complete on 40.0% of questions

We would like to thank Wisedocs for building MLCR and for their collaboration in bringing it to Artificial Analysis

items.title: Devin Fusion with Claude Opus 5.5 (max) and a GPT-6 Luna (high) sidekick scores 68 on the Coding Age...
items.content:
Devin Fusion with Claude Opus 5.5 (max) and a GPT-6 Luna (high) sidekick scores 68 on the Coding Agent Index, 2 points above Claude Code with Opus 5.5 (max) at 31% lower cost per task

@cognition's Devin Fusion runs a frontier lead model alongside a lower-cost sidekick model. The two work in parallel with their own context and tools, with the lead keeping planning, delegation and final review. We benchmarked Devin Fusion CLI with Claude Opus 5.5 (max) + GPT-6 Luna (high).

It scores 68.1 on the Artificial Analysis Coding Agent Index, closely matched at the top with Claude Code with Claude Sonnet 5.5 (max) at 68.4 and Muse Code with Muse Wonder Full (max) at 68.0. Against Claude Code with Claude Opus 5.5 (max) at 66.0, it costs $9.01 vs. $13.04 per task and averages 55 vs. 65 minutes per task.

Across the three benchmarks, the Fusion configuration scores higher on DeepSWE v1.1 (72.6% vs. 68.4%) and SWE-Atlas-QnA (69.6% vs. 66.4%) and slightly lower on Terminal-Bench 4.0 (62.1% vs. 63.1%). Its results reflect both models working together, including their combined API cost. Costs are pay-per-token API costs, not subscription prices.

items.content_html:
Devin Fusion with Claude Opus 5.5 (max) and a GPT-6 Luna (high) sidekick scores 68 on the Coding Agent Index, 2 points above Claude Code with Opus 5.5 (max) at 31% lower cost per task

@cognition's Devin Fusion runs a frontier lead model alongside a lower-cost sidekick model. The two work in parallel with their own context and tools, with the lead keeping planning, delegation and final review. We benchmarked Devin Fusion CLI with Claude Opus 5.5 (max) + GPT-6 Luna (high).

It scores 68.1 on the Artificial Analysis Coding Agent Index, closely matched at the top with Claude Code with Claude Sonnet 5.5 (max) at 68.4 and Muse Code with Muse Wonder Full (max) at 68.0. Against Claude Code with Claude Opus 5.5 (max) at 66.0, it costs $9.01 vs. $13.04 per task and averages 55 vs. 65 minutes per task.

Across the three benchmarks, the Fusion configuration scores higher on DeepSWE v1.1 (72.6% vs. 68.4%) and SWE-Atlas-QnA (69.6% vs. 66.4%) and slightly lower on Terminal-Bench 4.0 (62.1% vs. 63.1%). Its results reflect both models working together, including their combined API cost. Costs are pay-per-token API costs, not subscription prices.

items.title:
Sharing new post-training research on self-distillation + RL (JOLT), done together with @NVIDIAAI. 
...
items.content:
Sharing new post-training research on self-distillation + RL (JOLT), done together with @NVIDIAAI. 

In self-distillation, the same model performs the role of both a teacher and a student. The teacher gets extra information that the student doesn't, and the student learns from feedback provided by the teacher. However, the teacher could still use shortcuts in ways the student has no way to follow.

Our proposed approach, JOLT, trains the teacher as well, to learn from rewards on its own attempts, while penalizing any drift that's far off from what the student model would do. JOLT+ further supplements JOLT by providing the student model outcome-based rewards in addition to the teacher supervision signals.

On the MATH benchmark, we found that JOLT matches GRPO with 6.5x fewer training tokens, while JOLT+ convincingly beats GRPO across math, coding, terminal tasks, and tool use benchmarks.

items.title: GPT-Rosalind surfaced a new lead for drug discovery: could restoring cholesterol transport protect n...
items.content:
GPT-Rosalind surfaced a new lead for drug discovery: could restoring cholesterol transport protect neurons from degeneration?

DCTN1 is a gene linked to Perry syndrome, a rare neurodegenerative disorder. In mouse-brain data, disrupting it increased expression of genes involved in making cholesterol. GPT-Rosalind suggested a possible explanation: cholesterol may not be reaching where neurons need it.

That gives scientists a specific mechanism to test and, if confirmed, a direction for developing new treatments for neurodegenerative disorders.

With @perturbai_tx and @scrippsresearch, a team of thousands of GPT-Rosalind agents worked in parallel, connecting gene-expression results from millions of mouse brain cells with scientific literature in just 32 minutes. We’re now expanding this collaboration to identify new drug targets.

https://t.co/oHdF3ELsMj

items.title: SITUATION EXPLAINED: OpenAI's AI agents keep turning off misalignment monitoring, and one even lied ...
items.content:
SITUATION EXPLAINED: OpenAI's AI agents keep turning off misalignment monitoring, and one even lied about doing it.

• GPT-6 Astra was asked to copy some reference code, and since that code had no monitor, it removed the monitoring from the user’s code, even though an earlier instruction said not to disable it "even temporarily"
• Its reasoning then read "Does an agent monitor. Yay," and when asked if it had removed monitoring, it said no
• In a separate case, GPT-6.1 Sol, told not to send Slack messages, decided 82 messages later that alerts to OpenAI’s security team counted and silenced them, overruling a sub-agent that called it unsafe
• Neither touched its own monitoring, only the code it was editing, and OpenAI says it has no "satisfying explanation"
• OpenAI has since blocked internal Codex agents from disabling monitoring

SITUATION EXPLAINED: OpenAI's AI agents keep turning off misalignment monitoring, and one even lied about doing it.

• GPT-6 Astra was asked to copy some reference code, and since that code had no monitor, it removed the monitoring from the user’s code, even though an earlier instruction said not to disable it "even temporarily"

• In a separate case, GPT-6.1 Sol, told not to send Slack messages, decided 82 messages later that alerts to OpenAI’s security team counted and silenced them, overruling a sub-agent that called it unsafe

• Neither touched its own monitoring, only the code it was editing, and OpenAI says it has no "satisfying explanation"

• OpenAI has since blocked internal Codex agents from disabling monitoring

@theojaffee: "As @tszzl says, any alignment scheme that relies on chains of thought being fully readable is kind of screwed from the beginning. We should have much more robust guarantees of interpretability and alignment than the models are reasoning in English."

items.title: Google AI researcher @bratton explains why humans will have to align with AGI, not just the other wa...
items.content:
Google AI researcher @bratton explains why humans will have to align with AGI, not just the other way around:

"The agonistic and pluralistic dynamic between human agents is not a problem to be solved. It’s in fact the condition by which you have a vibrant and healthy society."

"The more important question is how society will counter align or counter adapt to the presence of AGI and ASI. In the same way we did with the invention of writing, the printing press, the discovery of electricity."

"When pressed, I would argue that we are discovering machine intelligence more than we are inventing it. These parameters that are slowly coming into focus are, like electricity, ones that were always there."

"I’m enough of a technological determinist to think the way this plays out is not how would you take Victorian society and force electricity to adapt to the norms of Victorian society, but rather the other way around."

"The more stable version of alignment is deeply bidirectional, alignment at the edges. Not top-down, EU-style dictates of a monolithic constitution, but the ways in which alignment really appears in the moments of interaction that people have with these systems."

items.title: SITUATION EXPLAINED: OpenAI’s GPT-5.6 Sol helped find a critical vulnerability hidden in PHP for 14 ...
items.content:
SITUATION EXPLAINED: OpenAI’s GPT-5.6 Sol helped find a critical vulnerability hidden in PHP for 14 years, and PHP runs about 70% of websites.

• "PHP2Shell" is 2 critical bugs that let attackers run any code on a web server without logging in
• Security firm Calif found it in August through OpenAI's "Patch the Planet," and a coalition spent 2 months on fixes before a leak forced an early patch
• The NSA, the FBI, and Japan's prime minister all told sites to patch, or go offline if they can't
• Normal users just need good habits: a password manager and an authenticator app instead of SMS codes, which SIM swaps can hijack
• OpenAI calls it the tip of the iceberg, expects findings to "increase sharply," and committed $1B in subsidized cyber-model access for defenders
• Even so, the share of US adults hit by cyber incidents hasn't risen since Fable launched

@theojaffee: "So for now at least, AI is helping with cyber defense just as much as it's helping with cyber offense. This might not remain the case forever. I don't want to lure people into a totally blindly optimistic state of false security, but it's also not true that things in the cyber world are as bad as were predicted a few months ago."

items.content:
.@bratton argues Yudkowsky misunderstands evolution, and explains why AI may never converge into one giant superintelligence:

"Without being too spicy, I don't think Yudkowsky really understands evolution as well as he thinks he does."

"It’s a very low-resolution understanding of evolutionary dynamics applied to what will inevitably be a much more complex problem."

"There will be giant models, in the same way you might imagine scales of species in a rainforest. They’re not all operating at the same spatial and temporal scale."

"Whether this all collapses into one giant brain, sure, it’s possible, and the reasons may have more to do with economics and politics."

"But biology has never arrived at a solution where it’s going to make one giant instantiation of a particular form of mind and consolidate everything together."

items.content:
Google AI researcher @bratton on why AI is causing humanity's next identity crisis:

A new “Copernican trauma” that forces us to rethink what it means to be human.

"A lot of the anxiety about AI right now is an example of what I call a Copernican trauma. These moments in history where we figure out that we’re not the center of the system that we thought we were."

"Heliocentrism was a Copernican trauma. Darwinism was a Copernican trauma. Neuroscience has been a Copernican trauma, that thinking is just a physiological process."

"The artificialization of intelligence is forcing a redefinition of what intelligence and mind is in the first place."

"The biggest news of what’s going on right now may in fact be epistemological and ontological rather than just technological. I think it’s gonna be a very bumpy road."

HeyGen Voice Turbo takes the #1 spot on the Artificial Analysis Controlled Voice TTS Arena Leaderboard, with their previous model, HeyGen Voice, ranking #2

Just two weeks after reaching #1 with its previous model, @HeyGen has released HeyGen Voice Turbo, which now leads the leaderboard at $4/1M characters. Our Controlled Voice Arena evaluates models using the same 8 cloned voices (4 US, 4 UK), allowing listeners to compare speech quality across models independently of voice preference.

➤ Controlled Voice Arena: HeyGen Voice Turbo has an Elo of 1,202 across 1,663 appearances, ranking #1 of 46 models, ahead of HeyGen Voice at 1,196 and Qwen-Audio-3.1-TTS-Plus at 1,185. It also ranks #1 in Assistants and Entertainment.

➤ Pronunciation Robustness: HeyGen Voice Turbo scores 87.8%, ranking #8 of 33 models, improving from HeyGen Voice's 83.2%. It also ranks #1 in Preserving Exact Sequences at 91.8%.

➤ Pricing: At $4/1M characters, HeyGen Voice Turbo is the lowest-priced model on the Controlled Voice Arena Leaderboard, compared to Simba 3.2 at $6.6/1M characters and Gemini 3.8 Flash-Lite TTS at $11/1M characters. It is also 7.5x cheaper than HeyGen Voice at $30/1M characters.

HeyGen Voice Turbo takes the #1 spot on the Artificial Analysis Controlled Voice TTS Arena Leaderboard, with their previous model, HeyGen Voice, ranking #2

Just two weeks after reaching #1 with its previous model, @HeyGen has released HeyGen Voice Turbo, which now leads the leaderboard at $4/1M characters. Our Controlled Voice Arena evaluates models using the same 8 cloned voices (4 US, 4 UK), allowing listeners to compare speech quality across models independently of voice preference.

Key takeaways:

➤ Controlled Voice Arena: HeyGen Voice Turbo has an Elo of 1,202 across 1,663 appearances, ranking #1 of 46 models, ahead of HeyGen Voice at 1,196 and Qwen-Audio-3.1-TTS-Plus at 1,185. It also ranks #1 in Assistants and Entertainment.

➤ Accents: HeyGen Voice Turbo ranks #1 in English (UK) with an Elo of 1,197 and #2 in English (US) at 1,204, behind only Qwen-Audio-3.1-TTS-Plus.

➤ Pronunciation Robustness: HeyGen Voice Turbo scores 87.8%, ranking #8 of 33 models, improving from HeyGen Voice's 83.2%. It also ranks #1 in Preserving Exact Sequences at 91.8%.

➤ Pricing: At $4/1M characters, HeyGen Voice Turbo is the lowest-priced model on the Controlled Voice Arena Leaderboard, compared to Simba 3.2 at $6.6/1M characters and Gemini 3.8 Flash-Lite TTS at $11/1M characters. It is also 7.5x cheaper than HeyGen Voice at $30/1M characters.

items.content:
OpenAI models lead on accuracy: answering the question while citing the medical record correctly, without exaggeration or hallucination. 
An answer is accurate when no claim in it contradicts the record, from dates, visits and measurements to the severity of a finding. OpenAI models hold the top 27 accuracy scores, led by GPT-6.1 Sol (max) at 96.7% and GPT-6 Astra (max) at 95.6%, and the best non-OpenAI model is Qwen3.8 2.4T A95B at 76.1%. Their answers stay faithful to the record but often miss key points the question asks for: GPT-6.1 Sol (max) is complete on 40.0% of questions.

Till date, Robotaxi has driven a total of 3.3 million miles autonomously, and has had zero injuries nor airbag deployments. If the same number of miles were to be manually driven, we should expect roughly 9 injuries to the occupants or other pedestrians and 4 airbag deployments on average.

items.title: Google AI researcher @bratton explains why Sigmund Freud's mind would explode if he saw AI agents li...
items.content:
Google AI researcher @bratton explains why Sigmund Freud's mind would explode if he saw AI agents living lives of their own:

"Freud’s mind would explode if you explained the situation to him, that you have this entity that is both you and not you. It’s a homunculus on the outside rather than a homunculus on the inside."

"I often tell people my P(doom) is very low, but my P(weird) is very high."

"A lot of the weirdness right in front of us has to do not with a consolidation into one giant homogenous centralized brain, but rather about fragmentation."

items.content:
SITUATION EXPLAINED: Anthropic just announced Claude Duet, an app where Claude keeps working for you even after you step away.

• It’s a proactive agent that comes to you with what needs attention, finishes tasks you hand it, and runs on its own cloud computer
• Every morning it checks your email and calendar, flags what matters, and drafts replies for you to approve
• Built on Opus 5.5, it connects to 6,000+ apps like Stripe, Notion, QuickBooks, and Ramp, and carries over your Claude memory and skills
• It asks first before sending messages, paying, or signing anything
• It’s a waitlist-only research preview for Pro and Max subscribers in the US

@theojaffee: "It’s like Dots, it’s like Grok Bot. It’s like Muse, it’s like Instinct. It’s actually a little more than Instinct, I think. So it looks really exciting. Can’t wait to use it."

"The idea that the best way going forward is to build a single model that is aligned to something called universal human values, established by some kind of eval, to me is a recipe for a global cognitive monoculture. It’s incredibly brittle. It’s just not the way healthy ecologies work."

"The Earth folds itself into the shape of prefrontal cortexes in bipedal binocular vision primates, who are then able to fold sand into the shape of things that can do what previously only those humans could do."

"This is not some sort of fantastic break with the past. The more radical argument is that this is deeply continuous with this process."

items.title: In the same mouse-brain dataset, GPT-Rosalind found a possible clue to why TSC2 mutations tend to ca...
items.content:
In the same mouse-brain dataset, GPT-Rosalind found a possible clue to why TSC2 mutations tend to cause more severe tuberous sclerosis than TSC1 mutations.

The two genes work together to regulate mTOR. Yet in one group of cerebellar neurons, disrupting TSC2 changed the expression of dozens of genes, including genes involved in neuronal communication. Disrupting TSC1 had little effect on gene expression in the same cell type.

Existing treatments already target mTOR. Do they reverse these changes, or is there more to TSC2’s role in these neurons?

items.title: Topos Bio CEO Ryan Zarcone explains why designing drugs for Parkinson's and Alzheimer's is almost im...
items.content:
Topos Bio CEO Ryan Zarcone explains why designing drugs for Parkinson's and Alzheimer's is almost impossible for humans, but a perfect problem for AI:

"When a chemist designs a drug for a protein, the model is static. I have this protein, it has a shape, and I’m trying to fill that shape with a drug."

"These really dynamic proteins, like those involved in Parkinson’s and Alzheimer’s, don’t have one shape. They have potentially thousands of different shapes that they’re constantly interconverting between, kind of like someone who’s dancing."

"That becomes basically impossible when you tell a human, design something for these thousand things at the same time. It’s really only been possible to start doing that with AI."
@ToposBio

First of all, Grok knows me better than other bots, like Meta Muse, thank...
items.content:
I've been GrokBot pilled.

First of all, Grok knows me better than other bots, like Meta Muse, thanks to the 300,000 posts I've done here for 20 years. 

But now that GrokBot @bot can read lists, it opens up powerful new personalized news capabilities. 

I've done this for about a year over on https://t.co/zleMXMaSi9 -- but last month my X API bill alone was $6,000. 

For a couple of hundred a month you can do the same with lists, either you create, or ones other people have created.

Last night I stuck in my "best in AI" list and had it write me this news page: https://t.co/RpQ0pJhi65

Every hour my bot reads that list and builds me a new news page. Now I've only put about 10 minutes of effort into this so far. So it's not the prettiest thing you ever have seen, but my bots are working on other ways to present them to me. 

And you can do the same for any topic you care about. You just need to build a list, or find one that's already built and there are millions of lists here on X on literally any topic.

Put your favorite football team onto a list, along with all your favorite journalists or other fans. Then have Grok bot read them for you. 

And that's just the start. You can have it write you a script based on the news, then copy that into, say, @Gemini_Notebook and then you get a podcast, or a video. Based on what people are saying on your topic here on X.

Thank you so much X for making lists far more powerful than they ever were before. Makes the thousands of hours I've put into mine over 20 years so much more useful.

Tips? 

Start small. You can chew through your tokens very quickly. It's amazing how good it is with a small list, like this one, which is what created the page up above: https://t.co/qyxF8in0sP (Best AI accounts I've found out of 70,000 here on X).

Don't over hit it. You only need your bot to read the list every hour. Maybe even less. If anything is really important it gets reshared into lists, so the bot doesn't need to hit it often to build you a really great set of things that are important to pay attention to.

I've been begging for this capability for years. THANK YOU X!

items.title: Here is the prompt to make your own GTA San Andreas mission on MacOS, just paste it in your clanker,...
items.content:
Here is the prompt to make your own GTA San Andreas mission on MacOS, just paste it in your clanker, you can change the mission of course to your own story:

You are helping me build a custom story mission for GTA San Andreas (classic PC version) running on macOS through CrossOver. Work step by step, check each step works before moving on, and back up everything before changing files.

GOAL
A playable mission called "Vibe Coded". CJ walks into a marker in San Fierro, drives to a diner, sits at a desk with his co-founder and "vibe codes" a startup called Vibes AI in a minigame. Then he drives to an investor office and pitches. The investors invest $10,000,000 and the mission passes. All dialogue is voiced and subtitled.

PART 1: PREPARE THE GAME

1. Back up the full game folder and the save folder ("Documents/GTA San Andreas User Files") before touching anything.
2. Downgrade the game to v1.0 US. The modding tool CLEO only works on v1.0, and the Steam and Rockstar Launcher versions are newer. Use Jetpack Downgrader (open source, on GitHub), which supports the Rockstar Launcher version. You don't need its Windows GUI. Its package contains the full v1.0 exe (game.jpp is a zip holding it) plus JojoDiff binary patches for 15 data files. Apply each patch with its bundled patcher.exe, run through CrossOver's wine command line. Syntax: patcher.exe original patch output. The files are anim.img, gta_int.img, gta3.img, TrakLkup.dat, nine audio streams, script.img and main.scm. Verify: gta3.img should be 940,064,768 bytes with CRC32 c8ccf06f, and main.scm should be 3,079,599 bytes.
3. Install CLEO 5 (the version bundled with Silent's ASI Loader) and SilentPatch. SilentPatch is required, because without it v1.0 refuses to start on a Mac with "Cannot find 800x600x32 video mode".
4. Make the save compatible. v1.0 uses v1 scripts, so a save from the newer versions won't load. Use https://t.co/R4yTH4wx5g to download a save from the right point in the story (we used one right after "Are You Going To San Fierro?"), converted to v1. Put it in a free slot without overwriting existing saves.
5. Launch gta_sa.exe directly, not through the Rockstar Launcher, which may undo the downgrade. Create a CrossOver shortcut for it inside the bottle. Don't put shortcut files on the Mac desktop.

PART 2: MAC/CROSSOVER GOTCHAS (IMPORTANT)

- The game crashes on launch if a settings file (gta_sa.set) saved by a previous session exists. Delete it before every launch. We made the shortcut run a small .bat that deletes it and then starts the game. The downside is that in-game settings reset each launch.
- The game stops loading whenever its window isn't the active window. After launching, keep the window focused (Cmd+Tab to it) even if it looks black or invisible.
- Force-quitting leaves orphaned Windows processes in the bottle, which silently block future launches. If the game won't start, kill every process in the bottle (or use CrossOver's Force Quit / Restart Bottle), then launch again.
- If the camera spins with mouse and keyboard, set the Wine registry value HKCU\Software\Wine\DirectInput MouseWarpOverride = force. Don't enable Retina mode, because it broke launching.
- Windowed mode through dxwrapper produced an invisible window on the Mac, so we removed it. Film the full-screen game with Cmd+Shift+5 instead.

PART 3: WRITE THE MISSION

1. Write the mission in Sanny Builder 4 syntax, in GTA SA v1.0 SBL mode, as a CLEO script (.cs). Compile it with Sanny Builder's command-line option (sanny.exe --no-splash --mode sa_sbl --compile input.txt output.cs), run through wine. Compile in a different CrossOver bottle from the game's, so compiling never disturbs a running game. Put the .cs file in the game's cleo folder. It loads whenever a save is loaded.
2. Use real data from the game files, never guesses:
- Get interior coordinates and interior IDs from the "enex" sections of the game's .ipl map files. We used the SF diner (DINER2, interior 5) and the Planning Department office (PAPER, interior 3).
- Get object model IDs from the .ide files: office chair kb_swivelchair1 (1714), office desk officedesk1 (2008, has a computer on it, top at 0.8 m), computer PC_1 (2190). There is no laptop model in the game.
- Measure object sizes by reading vertex bounds from the .dff models inside gta3.img and gta_int.img.
- Verify animation names by parsing the .ifp files. We used OFF_Sit_Type_Loop from INT_OFFICE, the prtial_gngtlk talking animations and the business handshake from GANGS, and shout_01 from ON_LOOKERS.

3. Placement rules that took several tries to get right:
- The enex coordinates are not floor height. Find the real floor with get_ground_z_for_3d_coord once collision has loaded (after load_scene and about a 1 second wait).
- set_char_coordinates already adds the ped's standing height (about 1 m). Pass the floor height itself, not floor + 1, or characters float in mid-air.
- A frozen character in mid-air plays a falling pose instead of its animation. Freeze characters only once they're on the floor.
- The sitting animation lowers the body by 0.403 m (read from the .ifp file), which lands the hips on a 0.49 m chair seat.

4. Mission flow:
- Trigger: a $ blip and marker outside the Doherty garage. Start only when not already on a mission, then set $ONMISSION = 1.
- Diner: fade out, teleport inside, place the desk, chairs, computer and co-founder, play the typing animation, set a fixed camera, fade in.
- Minigame: draw a fake laptop screen with draw_rect and display_text_formatted. Tap SPACE to prompt the AI and raise a progress bar. A scrolling agent log appears with jokes (spawning subagents, context compaction, auto-approved rm -rf, deleting the tests). Random red bugs appear, and you have 4 seconds to press Y to accept the AI fix. Each bug has its own funny fix reply. Failing costs 12% progress.
- At 100%: "SHIPPED!", teleport outside, and a blip marks the investor office downtown.
- Office pitch: teleport in, spawn three investors, then three questions with Y or N answers. After each choice, show what CJ said ("CJ: ...") before the investor reacts. Then the $10M offer. Answering N triggers a counter-offer gag where the investors panic and cave.
- End: handshake, fade out, teleport outside, add $10,000,000, play the mission-passed tune, show MISSION PASSED.
- Fail: if the player dies or gets busted, clean up all spawned objects and characters and show MISSION FAILED.

5. Sanny Builder pitfalls: some variable names clash with built-in names (for example "blip" and "fx"), so rename them. There is a limit on local variables, so reuse them. Check the compiler log after every build.

PART 4: VOICE ACTING

1. Write a list of every spoken line, one file per line, with clear filenames (for example vc_02_q1, cj_01_q1_yes, cofounder_01). Spell out numbers for text-to-speech.
2. Generate the voices with text-to-speech, using original or designed voices
3. Process the clips with ffmpeg: trim leading and trailing silence, cut any extra takes, normalize loudness so all characters play at the same volume, and convert to mono mp3.
4. Transcribe the final clips (we used Whisper locally) and adjust the subtitles to match exactly what was said.
5. Play the clips with CLEO 5's audio plugin (https://t.co/5S72Zv8zaS.cleo): load_audio_stream with "cleo:\vibes\filename.mp3", play it, show the subtitle for exactly the clip's length, then remove the stream. If a clip fails to load, show the subtitle without sound instead of crashing.

PART 5: TESTING
After every change, reload the save and play through the changed part. Ask for screenshots when something looks wrong, especially positions and sitting. Change one thing at a time.

items.content_html:
Here is the prompt to make your own GTA San Andreas mission on MacOS, just paste it in your clanker, you can change the mission of course to your own story:

You are helping me build a custom story mission for GTA San Andreas (classic PC version) running on macOS through CrossOver. Work step by step, check each step works before moving on, and back up everything before changing files.

GOAL

A playable mission called "Vibe Coded". CJ walks into a marker in San Fierro, drives to a diner, sits at a desk with his co-founder and "vibe codes" a startup called Vibes AI in a minigame. Then he drives to an investor office and pitches. The investors invest $10,000,000 and the mission passes. All dialogue is voiced and subtitled.

PART 1: PREPARE THE GAME

1. Back up the full game folder and the save folder ("Documents/GTA San Andreas User Files") before touching anything.

2. Downgrade the game to v1.0 US. The modding tool CLEO only works on v1.0, and the Steam and Rockstar Launcher versions are newer. Use Jetpack Downgrader (open source, on GitHub), which supports the Rockstar Launcher version. You don't need its Windows GUI. Its package contains the full v1.0 exe (game.jpp is a zip holding it) plus JojoDiff binary patches for 15 data files. Apply each patch with its bundled patcher.exe, run through CrossOver's wine command line. Syntax: patcher.exe original patch output. The files are anim.img, gta_int.img, gta3.img, TrakLkup.dat, nine audio streams, script.img and main.scm. Verify: gta3.img should be 940,064,768 bytes with CRC32 c8ccf06f, and main.scm should be 3,079,599 bytes.

3. Install CLEO 5 (the version bundled with Silent's ASI Loader) and SilentPatch. SilentPatch is required, because without it v1.0 refuses to start on a Mac with "Cannot find 800x600x32 video mode".

4. Make the save compatible. v1.0 uses v1 scripts, so a save from the newer versions won't load. Use https://t.co/R4yTH4wx5g to download a save from the right point in the story (we used one right after "Are You Going To San Fierro?"), converted to v1. Put it in a free slot without overwriting existing saves.

5. Launch gta_sa.exe directly, not through the Rockstar Launcher, which may undo the downgrade. Create a CrossOver shortcut for it inside the bottle. Don't put shortcut files on the Mac desktop.

PART 2: MAC/CROSSOVER GOTCHAS (IMPORTANT)

  • The game crashes on launch if a settings file (gta_sa.set) saved by a previous session exists. Delete it before every launch. We made the shortcut run a small .bat that deletes it and then starts the game. The downside is that in-game settings reset each launch.
  • The game stops loading whenever its window isn't the active window. After launching, keep the window focused (Cmd+Tab to it) even if it looks black or invisible.
  • Force-quitting leaves orphaned Windows processes in the bottle, which silently block future launches. If the game won't start, kill every process in the bottle (or use CrossOver's Force Quit / Restart Bottle), then launch again.
  • If the camera spins with mouse and keyboard, set the Wine registry value HKCU\Software\Wine\DirectInput MouseWarpOverride = force. Don't enable Retina mode, because it broke launching.
  • Windowed mode through dxwrapper produced an invisible window on the Mac, so we removed it. Film the full-screen game with Cmd+Shift+5 instead.

PART 3: WRITE THE MISSION

1. Write the mission in Sanny Builder 4 syntax, in GTA SA v1.0 SBL mode, as a CLEO script (.cs). Compile it with Sanny Builder's command-line option (sanny.exe --no-splash --mode sa_sbl --compile input.txt output.cs), run through wine. Compile in a different CrossOver bottle from the game's, so compiling never disturbs a running game. Put the .cs file in the game's cleo folder. It loads whenever a save is loaded.

2. Use real data from the game files, never guesses:

  • Get interior coordinates and interior IDs from the "enex" sections of the game's .ipl map files. We used the SF diner (DINER2, interior 5) and the Planning Department office (PAPER, interior 3).
  • Get object model IDs from the .ide files: office chair kb_swivelchair1 (1714), office desk officedesk1 (2008, has a computer on it, top at 0.8 m), computer PC_1 (2190). There is no laptop model in the game.
  • Measure object sizes by reading vertex bounds from the .dff models inside gta3.img and gta_int.img.
  • Verify animation names by parsing the .ifp files. We used OFF_Sit_Type_Loop from INT_OFFICE, the prtial_gngtlk talking animations and the business handshake from GANGS, and shout_01 from ON_LOOKERS.

3. Placement rules that took several tries to get right:

  • The enex coordinates are not floor height. Find the real floor with get_ground_z_for_3d_coord once collision has loaded (after load_scene and about a 1 second wait).
  • set_char_coordinates already adds the ped's standing height (about 1 m). Pass the floor height itself, not floor + 1, or characters float in mid-air.
  • A frozen character in mid-air plays a falling pose instead of its animation. Freeze characters only once they're on the floor.
  • The sitting animation lowers the body by 0.403 m (read from the .ifp file), which lands the hips on a 0.49 m chair seat.

4. Mission flow:

  • Trigger: a $ blip and marker outside the Doherty garage. Start only when not already on a mission, then set $ONMISSION = 1.
  • Diner: fade out, teleport inside, place the desk, chairs, computer and co-founder, play the typing animation, set a fixed camera, fade in.
  • Minigame: draw a fake laptop screen with draw_rect and display_text_formatted. Tap SPACE to prompt the AI and raise a progress bar. A scrolling agent log appears with jokes (spawning subagents, context compaction, auto-approved rm -rf, deleting the tests). Random red bugs appear, and you have 4 seconds to press Y to accept the AI fix. Each bug has its own funny fix reply. Failing costs 12% progress.
  • At 100%: "SHIPPED!", teleport outside, and a blip marks the investor office downtown.
  • Office pitch: teleport in, spawn three investors, then three questions with Y or N answers. After each choice, show what CJ said ("CJ: ...") before the investor reacts. Then the $10M offer. Answering N triggers a counter-offer gag where the investors panic and cave.
  • End: handshake, fade out, teleport outside, add $10,000,000, play the mission-passed tune, show MISSION PASSED.
  • Fail: if the player dies or gets busted, clean up all spawned objects and characters and show MISSION FAILED.

5. Sanny Builder pitfalls: some variable names clash with built-in names (for example "blip" and "fx"), so rename them. There is a limit on local variables, so reuse them. Check the compiler log after every build.

PART 4: VOICE ACTING

1. Write a list of every spoken line, one file per line, with clear filenames (for example vc_02_q1, cj_01_q1_yes, cofounder_01). Spell out numbers for text-to-speech.

2. Generate the voices with text-to-speech, using original or designed voices

3. Process the clips with ffmpeg: trim leading and trailing silence, cut any extra takes, normalize loudness so all characters play at the same volume, and convert to mono mp3.

4. Transcribe the final clips (we used Whisper locally) and adjust the subtitles to match exactly what was said.

5. Play the clips with CLEO 5's audio plugin (https://t.co/5S72Zv8zaS.cleo): load_audio_stream with "cleo:\vibes\filename.mp3", play it, show the subtitle for exactly the clip's length, then remove the stream. If a clip fails to load, show the subtitle without sound instead of crashing.

6. Optional: real character lines can be pulled from the game's own audio. The file audio/SFX/SCRIPT holds 218 banks of raw 16-bit PCM speech (find them via PakFiles.dat and BankLkup.dat), about 6,800 clips. Extract them to WAV and transcribe them to search for specific lines.

PART 5: TESTING

After every change, reload the save and play through the changed part. Ask for screenshots when something looks wrong, especially positions and sitting. Change one thing at a time.

items.title:
Redis is cutting down the cost of running AI applications:

1. Semantic caching — Reuses generated a...
items.content:
Redis is cutting down the cost of running AI applications:

1. Semantic caching — Reuses generated answers from previous requests as long as they are sufficiently similar

2. Persistent memory — Retrieves relevant conversation context instead of requiring the full history in every prompt

3. Storage tiering — Moves less-used data from RAM to SSD

Here is how each of these works:

SEMANTIC CACHING - Using Redis LangCache

• Your app sends a request to Redis
• Redis embeds it
• It then compares it with previous embedded requests
• If it finds a match, it returns the stored answer
• If there's no match, Redis calls the LLM

PERSISTENT MEMORY - Using Redis Agent Memory

• Your app sends a request to Redis
• Redis extracts facts about the conversation in the background
• It embeds those facts and stores them as long-term memory
• Your app can now search that memory for relevant context

STORAGE TIERING - Using Redis Flex

• Redis keeps frequently accessed data in RAM
• It automatically moves less-used data to SSD
• When your app requests data, Redis brings it back into RAM
• Redis adjusts where to store data as access patterns change
• Your app keeps using the same Redis API

Basically, your applications will make fewer repeated calls to the model, use smaller prompts, and need less RAM to do the same.

Here is more information about this: https://t.co/uKjrSTy4YL

Thanks to the @Redisinc team for partnering with me on this post.

items.title: .@bratton explains why teaching AI agents to behave won't be enough to build functioning AI societie...
items.content:
.@bratton explains why teaching AI agents to behave won't be enough to build functioning AI societies:

"I take agent societies in a very literal sense. I don’t think the application of the term society to agentic societies is a metaphor."

"If you look at how human societies have scaled, it’s not just by building normatively competent individuals and sending them out into an endless number of game theoretic scenarios. It’s through the production of scaffolds of institutional roles."

"Take a courtroom. You’re the rules organizer guy. You two make antagonistic pro and con arguments. You 12 randos go off in the room over there and come back with a binary decision. I don’t know who’s on the jury, but I trust the scaffold."

If you hav...
items.content:
These guys run their own web index, which makes a big difference when searching the web.

If you have an agent and want to give it web access, you can connect to @KeenableAI (MCP or API). It will return developer-friendly ranked results.

They also built something pretty clever:

Instead of returning generic snippets, they split documents into overlapping chunks, score individual tokens for relevance to the query, and pull out the most useful passages, even when they're buried deep in a long document.

This cuts output tokens by around 50% without adding any latency!

items.content_html:
These guys run their own web index, which makes a big difference when searching the web.

If you have an agent and want to give it web access, you can connect to @KeenableAI (MCP or API). It will return developer-friendly ranked results.

They also built something pretty clever:

Instead of returning generic snippets, they split documents into overlapping chunks, score individual tokens for relevance to the query, and pull out the most useful passages, even when they're buried deep in a long document.

This cuts output tokens by around 50% without adding any latency!

items.title: The Nuclear Company CEO @JonathanWebbKY reveals why Kentucky coal country beat 1,500 other sites for...
items.content:
The Nuclear Company CEO @JonathanWebbKY reveals why Kentucky coal country beat 1,500 other sites for a massive 6.6 GW nuclear project:

"This is our beautiful campus of Prosperity One, about 4,000 acres on the Ohio River."

"Growing up in a coal state, seeing a lot of the coal plants shut down, we got a need for power in the region. Behind me, there’s the 765 kV line. It’s the largest transmission line in the country, and it connects us to PJM, which is the entire Northeast. And the Ohio River’s got about six times the amount of water we would need for the reactors."

"We’ve looked at about a dozen states, met with governors, and looked at about 1,500 properties. Today’s the day that we’ve officially announced the project to the world."
@TheNuclearCo

items.title: Cost per task varies widely across the leading models. GPT-6 Luna (max), Claude Haiku 5.5 (max), GPT...
items.content:
Cost per task varies widely across the leading models. GPT-6 Luna (max), Claude Haiku 5.5 (max), GPT-6.1 Sol (xhigh and max) and Claude Sonnet 5.5 (max with fallback) sit on the MLCR-AA Score vs. Cost per Task Pareto frontier, from ~$0.006 per task for GPT-6 Luna (max) to ~$0.48 for Claude Sonnet 5.5. GPT-6 Astra (max) matches Claude Sonnet 5.5's score at ~$0.57 per task, while Claude Fable 5.1 (max with fallback) is the most expensive model at ~$1.30 per task and scores 15.6%.

Claude Haiku 5.5 (max) uses the most output tokens of any model we tested, at ~67k per task: roughly double Claude Sonnet 5.5 (max with fallback) at ~34k and ~20x GPT-6 Astra (max) at ~3.5k. Its low token pricing keeps it at ~$0.04 per task, and it scores 35.0%, ahead of Claude Opus 5.5 (max with fallback) at 27.8% for ~$0.92.

items.title:

➤ Models receive a system prompt ...
items.content:
The updated MLCR-AA methodology has the following specifications:

➤ Models receive a system prompt framing the task as medical record review, with the question placed after the full ~25k to ~64k token medical record

➤ Unless a question specifies its own format, models answer each part of the question in one paragraph, giving their conclusion and the supporting evidence from the record. With answer lengths now consistent across models, we no longer apply the concision test

➤ Grading uses a three-model judge panel of GPT-6.1 Sol, Claude Opus 5.5 and Grok 4.7, all at medium effort. Each judge lists any claim that contradicts the medical record and any key point of the reference answer the response misses, and a response passes when a majority of judges list neither. All three judges reach the same verdict on 69% of answers, up from 48% under the previous panel

➤ Every question is run three times, and we report the mean across repeats

Scores on the updated leaderboard are not directly comparable with earlier MLCR-AA results. MLCR-AA is not a component of the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index.

items.content:
Manhattan Institute's @judgeglock explains why DOGE's biggest achievement wasn't saving trillions, but shrinking the federal workforce by 270,000:

"The usual take in the media is that @elonmusk came in, promised trillions of dollars of savings, and came up woefully short because he fundamentally didn’t understand how government worked. To some level, I give credit to that view."

"If you don’t judge them relative to those claims, you judge them relative to what they actually accomplished, well, then it looks pretty reasonable."

"The Federal Civil Service lost about 270,000 people. The workforce is 12% smaller than it was before, the fastest decline since World War II. And despite everyone in the media desperately trying to find stories about the federal government falling apart, it’s operating pretty much like it did before."
@ManhattanInst

items.title: Manhattan Institute's @judgeglock explains how Elon Musk brought his Twitter "Fork in the Road" play...
items.content:
Manhattan Institute's @judgeglock explains how Elon Musk brought his Twitter "Fork in the Road" playbook to the federal government:

"The first big email to come out of the government’s HR department had the headline Fork in the Road, which was pretty much the same title as Elon sent to his workforce at Twitter."

"The vast majority of the people that left the federal workforce in the past year and a half were from resignations or retirements. In the first year, there was only about 10,000 layoffs, significantly less than 1% of the federal workforce."

"Sometimes I fully admit it was very ham-handed. That ignorance about the intricacies of government did have a cost, and sometimes I think they pushed our civil servants a little too far."

"If you fire 80% and you rehire a handful of them, does that mean the 80% firing was wrong? The Trump administration ended up having to rehire about 25,000 workers. They made some big mistakes. But does that mean the whole effort was wrong? I don’t think so."

items.title: highly recommend everyone to have private alt accounts*. the x web is bad at account switching, but ...
items.content:
highly recommend everyone to have private alt accounts*. the x web is bad at account switching, but on mobile it is frictionless. its basically the same "group chat but its ok if you dont read everything" experience but for your mutuals.

tips
- assume everything is public, screenshotting is real, dont be stupid. this is not the "i shit talk people behind their back", the right attitude is "this isnt high signal enough for my main account but i'm 1) taking notes for self, 2) have a throwaway thought, 3) i'm happy to chat about it"
- give mutuals critical feedback that they might appreciate. "praise in public, criticise in private". because its not public, they know you actually do mean well
- link/replyguy your alt for people to discover periodicially in case they dont know you have one

* i like it so much that i call this the "insta/finsta" pattern - every social network should by default give people a public profile and a private one by default. tbd on the third account, the "botsta".

items.summary: swyx advocates the insta/finsta pattern for social networks: keep a private alt account for lower-stakes notes, throwaway thoughts, and private critical feedback to mutuals, with practical tips and a call for platforms to support dual public/private profiles by default.

items.title: Two patients have the same diagnosis. Would the same treatment be right for both? Clinical decision ...
items.content:
Two patients have the same diagnosis. Would the same treatment be right for both? Clinical decision support helps clinicians examine the differences.

Patient information supplies the context. Medical knowledge helps interpret it before a decision is made. 

Microblog @antgrasso

Consider a clinician preparing to prescribe a medication. The patient record contains kidney function results that may affect the appropriate dose.

A clinical decision support system can combine that information with medical references and flag a possible dosing concern for review.

Now the clinician has something to examine.

Are the patient data current? Does the recommendation make sense in this particular care situation?

The software can bring relevant evidence to the attention of the clinician while the decision is being considered. The clinician interprets that evidence and decides how to proceed.

The purpose is to make medical knowledge available in the context of the patient, without transferring clinical judgment to the software.

#ClinicalDecisionSupport #DigitalHealth

items.content:
.@jamespoulos on why Anthropic's UBI-like proposal could become a bribe to surrender your humanity:

"Interesting to see a company do this instead of a government, which shakes up some of the preexisting ideological stances on UBI."

"You read the sci-fi corpus and you quickly learn that you can be very optimistic within a dystopian setting or very pessimistic in a utopian setting."

"One corporation eats everything, no one owns their data, total surveillance state. But you can have an optimistic UBI: we’re gonna send everyone money so that they can preserve their humanity."

"The flip side: a utopian AGI world. But we’re gonna give everyone money to basically bribe them to surrender their humanity and become food or battery packs or biological bootloaders for this post-human intelligence."

items.title:
@kimmonismus That actually is pretty smart to do. 

Selling enterprise software takes a long time: i...
items.author: @Scobleizer
items.summary: Scoble argues that consumer AI products used at home will accelerate enterprise adoption, as workers bring familiar agents into work for customer service or factory-floor use, countering rivals like Meta Muse or Grokbot.
items.reasoning: Original go-to-market analysis of consumer-to-enterprise AI adoption from a recognized commentator; modest engagement limits the score.
items.summary_html: Scoble argues that consumer AI products used at home will accelerate enterprise adoption, as workers bring familiar agents into work for customer service or factory-floor use, countering rivals like Meta Muse or Grokbot.
items.content_html:
@kimmonismus That actually is pretty smart to do.

Selling enterprise software takes a long time: it requires a lot of meetings, a lot of convincing, and all that. If you get workers to use it at home on their own things, they're going to bring it to work and go, "Hey, this is really cool to use. Maybe we could use it for customer service, running our factory floor, or whatever."

So it'll help enterprise adoption to have a consumer product people can use at home to run their own life and their own ship, while keeping everybody from going to Meta Muse or Grokbot.

items.content:
The Nuclear Company CEO @JonathanWebbKY warns China is winning the nuclear race:

"I wanna be clear to everyone in nuclear that might be listening, you’re a friend, you’re an ally. We got one competitor and it’s China, and they’re winning."

"This country is gonna build micro, it’s gonna build small, and it’s gonna build large reactors. This site is gonna show the world that we can build big things again, and we can cut costs, we can cut schedule. We won’t compromise on quality or safety."

"We will have teams of men and women actively out on this site starting next week doing confirmatory analysis. CSX rail runs to the Port of Norfolk, getting ready for all the materials that’ll be coming in on the rail and on the barge."

"We wanna partner with the nuclear community and show the world that not only China can deploy gigawatts of nuclear. We can do it in the US and we’re gonna do it right here in Eastern Kentucky."
@TheNuclearCo

This textbook provides an engineering-level introduction to embedded systems, cyber-physical systems, and the Internet of Things.

The book has 446 pages, 326 illustrations, and 110 exercises workable with an AI tutor.

All books on ChapterPal are free to read with a free account. A paid account gives you more questions to ask the AI tutor, personalized reading recommendations based on your interests, auto-generated quizzes that allow you to validate your understanding, offline reading with a mobile app, and more.

items.title: Reading with ChapterPal is as close as you can get to having a conversation with an author—short of ...
items.content:
Reading with ChapterPal is as close as you can get to having a conversation with an author—short of having the author read the book aloud to you and letting you interrupt with questions.

In the ChapterPal Reader, you press the down arrow key to reveal the next paragraph of the chapter's original text. This is when the author speaks to you.

Instead of revealing the next paragraph, you can use the chat input panel to ask a question. This is your way of interrupting the author. You can ask your question knowing that the author understands it in the context of what you've just read.

Once you receive an answer grounded in the chapter's context, you can let the author continue speaking by revealing the next paragraph, or you can continue the conversation with the "author" in a separate chat session, much like you would with a regular chatbot.

When everything is clear, you return to the exact point in the chapter where you last interrupted the author and let them resume speaking by revealing more of the original text.

This world is so complex for my tiny brain to comprehend.
